This mom is feeding a baby eight times heavier than she is.
Meet the reed warbler. She builds a nest, lays four eggs, and flies off to find food.
When she comes back, there are five.
One is a little bigger. She doesn't notice.
A cuckoo sneaked in, laid that egg in about ten seconds, and flew away forever.
Twelve days later, the big egg hatches first.
And the baby, blind, naked, just hours old, does something horrible.
It pushes every other egg out of the nest. One. By. One.
Now it's the only baby. And mom feeds it anyway.
But here's the thing. It's huge. It looks nothing like her. So why doesn't she notice?
The cuckoo chick doesn't sound like one baby. It sounds like a whole nest of hungry babies.
So she works like she has four. Day and night.
Until her baby is too big to fit in the nest.
Then one day, it just flies away. All the way to Africa.
And next spring? She builds a new nest. And lays four eggs.
